clue.text: Guard the stronghold temporarily

parts.note: read literally, a soldier keeping watch over a castle; the idiom means taking charge for a while until someone returns

explanation.surface: A sentry is told to keep watch over the castle for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to look after things on someone else's behalf for a short spell, as a garrison once kept a castle.

clue.text: Livery of the cap I dragged around

indicators.note: letters dragged around are pulled out of place and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's uniform includes a cap that has been dragged about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Livery' looks like a uniform, but here it means 'like the liver'; 'dragged around' rearranges THE CAP I.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective for anything to do with the liver, which is exactly what the medical term describes.

clue.text: Former Soviet leader came up on the 9.50

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the figure 9 spelt out is NINE and 50 is L in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Soviet politician arrived on a particular train time.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9.50' looks like a train timetable entry; 'came up' turns NINE plus L (Roman fifty) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Bolshevik revolution and was the first head of the Soviet state.

clue.text: Permitted variation of unusually clear note

indicators.note: letters arranged unusually are set out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An engineer allows some leeway for a note that is unusually clear.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, the allowed margin by which a measurement may differ from its nominal value.

clue.text: Wrong to be turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to be means to exist, to live

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to keep arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' looks like arriving, but it reverses LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or moral badness, as a noun or adjective synonym of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Consciously defeat opponent in the ring

definitions.text: Consciously defeat opponent in the ring

parts.words: Consciously defeat opponent in the ring
parts.note: a boxer who wins while the beaten rival stays conscious has won on the judges' scorecards rather than by knockout

explanation.definitionFit: To beat a boxer on the judges' scoring, so the loser is not knocked unconscious.

clue.text: Head-band, it turned up on an artist

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the little word is written bottom to top

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist appears wearing a band on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses IT to TI; A and RA (Royal Academician) follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Professional entertainer in part is terrible

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A performer, in one role, is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you to look inside 'part is terrible'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer, especially a singer or dancer, paid for the work.

clue.text: Unvarying quantity frequently occurring

definitions.meaning: in maths and science, a fixed value that does not change

explanation.definitionFit: Both a fixed value in an equation and an adjective for something continual or recurring.

clue.text: Penal reform group with printout for member of the jury

indicators.note: to reform and group the letters is to put them together in a new order

parts.note: a printed list, such as a computer printout

explanation.surface: A campaign for prison reform produces a printout naming a juror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform group' looks like a penal-reform campaign, but it rearranges PENAL into PANEL; LIST (printout) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting on a judging panel, such as a quiz or talent-show jury.

clue.text: Concerning sailor not being at home

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor
someone not at home is out

explanation.surface: Worry about a sailor who is never home.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition synonym, meaning on the subject of, regarding.

clue.text: Holding tangled net by the river

indicators.note: a tangled net has its letters twisted out of order

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An angler keeps a tangled net beside the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges NET into TEN; URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Possession or occupation of land or a post, a noun sense of holding.

clue.text: After a little while girls can be sweet

indicators.note: after means the girls come later than the short time in the word order

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a little while
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Give the girls a little time and they can turn sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark syrup from sugar refining, a sweet substance.

clue.text: Many doing badly using ciphers

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: letters arranged badly are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Lots of people perform poorly when working with secret codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing messages in secret code, the act of encrypting.

clue.text: Overhead scales?

parts.note: not weighing machines on a ceiling but flaky skin from the scalp, scales on top of the head

explanation.definitionFit: Flakes of dead skin shed from the scalp, scales on the head.

clue.text: Grow in line

parts.note: a crease is a line, a fold in cloth or paper

explanation.surface: Plants grow in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, to become bigger or more numerous.

clue.text: Back row to put in order again

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: The back row should be sorted out again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out again in a different sequence.

clue.text: Worn out garment

parts.note: not a threadbare piece of clothing but one worn outdoors, over everything else

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy coat put on over other clothes when going outdoors.

clue.text: Keep many on to work in a restaurant

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
a waiter's job is to serve

explanation.surface: Retain many staff to wait at tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, to preserve or save from loss.

clue.text: With no end of luck, many contrived malicious misrepresentation

indicators.note: contrived letters are artfully put together in a new arrangement
with no end means the last letter of the next word is dropped

explanation.surface: Without luck, lots of people cooked up a spiteful lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no end of' trims LUCK to LUC; 'contrived' rearranges LUC plus MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander: a false statement made to damage someone's reputation.

clue.text: First Michaelmas daisy for teacher

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower, the Michaelmas daisy

explanation.surface: The first Michaelmas daisy is picked for the teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' takes M from 'Michaelmas'; Michaelmas daisy is the British name for an aster.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster, a male teacher in a school.

clue.text: Either way undertake domestic hanging

indicators.note: either way means the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, do the household decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic hanging' is wallpapering, not an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up fresh wallpaper on the walls of a room.

clue.text: Left a wild pig in its own fat

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A wild pig is left stewing in its own fat.
explanation.walkthrough: BOAR goes inside LARD after LAR. The answer is an old nautical word for the port side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The old nautical term for port, the left-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: On account of being in debt

definitions.meaning: because of, as in due to circumstances

explanation.definitionFit: Both a phrase meaning because of and an adjective for money still unpaid.

clue.text: Stumble when the journey has finished

parts.note: a trip is a journey
when time is up it has finished

explanation.surface: Someone falls over at the end of the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to catch one's foot and nearly fall, or to make a mistake.

clue.text: Ground for Irishman next to the church

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock name for an Irishman
CH is an abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An Irishman has a plot of land beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of land, a plot.

clue.text: Commission a soldier with love

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An officer commissions a soldier with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' is a fee, not a military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker's fee or premium charged for changing money.

clue.text: Greek character has terrible fit in ordinary clothes

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: a terrible fit means the letters are badly out of place

explanation.surface: A Greek has a fit in his everyday clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain civilian dress worn by someone who normally wears uniform.

clue.text: But, however, it brings the musical instrument into action

definitions.text: But, however, it brings the musical instrument into action

parts.words: But, however, it brings the musical instrument into action
parts.note: the paradox is a device named for halting that actually lets a set of pipes sound when it is pulled out

explanation.definitionFit: A knob on a pipe organ that, when drawn, admits air to a rank of pipes.

clue.text: Achieve one's full potential without it gathering

indicators.note: without means the small word is taken out

parts.note: to get it together is to sort oneself out and reach one's potential

explanation.surface: Someone fulfils their promise without a social occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes IT from the idiom 'get it together'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal social meeting or party.
